body:
# Independent audit: proper critical three-fiber BM margin

Audited source:
`candidate 9f6a0ee7f33d8c84`.
Result: PASS as a scoped theorem. Its assumptions do not cover general OC.

## 1. Measure and scope

A,K,B are positive d-dimensional compact convex bodies, separated at integer
coordinates -1,0,1. Thus dim_H(S)=d and H_d(S)=|A|+|K|+|B| is finite and
positive, with standard Hausdorff normalization. Every cap mass is exactly
a three-term d-dimensional volume sum. No ambient (d+1)-volume is used.
The source explicitly assumes d>=2 and exactly these three fibers. Its
exclusions of d=1, zero-volume fibers, and additional fibers are legitimate
scope restrictions, not assertions that those cases follow.

The selected point is the given (0,y), which belongs to S. Global maximality
of its depth is not assumed or used. Every listed cap attains the infimum
over all closed ambient halfspaces through or containing this source.

## 2. Integer-tilt derivative

For a fixed nonzero u, a proper endpoint cut level lies in the interior of
the body's u-projection interval. Its section has positive finite
(d-1)-area. Brunn--Minkowski for the sections makes the 1/(d-1) power of
the section area concave and therefore continuous on that open interval.
Fubini in coordinates u/|u| gives precisely

    F_D'(t)=-sigma_D(t)/|u|.

With the source held fixed, the middle capture is independent of alpha,
the A threshold is u.y+alpha, and the B threshold is u.y-alpha. Hence the
mass derivative is (-sigma_A+sigma_B)/|u|. A depth-attaining cap minimizes
this differentiable function over every real alpha, so the derivative
vanishes. This is an actual family of ambient halfspaces and includes
oblique integer/continuous coupling. No restricted-direction optimization
is substituted for the depth definition.

## 3. Exact captured BM and equal cap volumes

The midpoint of the endpoint captured bodies is contained in the middle
captured body. All three are full-dimensional because both endpoint cuts
are proper. The numerical root equality forces equality throughout the
BM/inclusion chain. Ordinary BM equality yields a positive homothety of
the endpoint cap bodies.

Each artificial cut section is exactly the minimum-u exposed face of its
cap body, and has positive (d-1)-area. A positive homothety takes this
exposed face to the corresponding exposed face. Its area scales by
lambda^(d-1), so section-area equality forces lambda=1 because d>=2.
The endpoint volumes are equal, and the numerical midpoint-root equality
makes the middle volume equal to them. The common cap mass Q therefore
implies that every listed middle cap has volume q=Q/3>0.

The middle cut is proper: select interior points on both strict sides of
each proper endpoint cut and take their midpoints. Midpoints on both
strict sides lie in K, so each side has positive K-volume. Therefore
q<|K|. This also verifies that no full/empty middle status was silently
assumed. Supporting or empty endpoint statuses are excluded explicitly;
the derivative proof is not claimed to handle them.

## 4. Cover, whole volumes, and exact constant

The finite middle cover contains the ordinary centroid in at least one
trace. Closed-halfspace Grünbaum applies even if the centroid is on the
cutting plane, and its d-volume boundary is zero. Since all middle cap
volumes equal q, this proves q>=Gamma_d |K|. The centroid is used solely
for this scalar inequality; the selected mixed point remains (0,y).

Writing a=|A|^(1/d),b=|B|^(1/d),c=|K|^(1/d),k=q^(1/d), actual midpoint
inclusion and whole-body BM give a+b<=2c. Cap containment gives a,b>=k.
Saturating the sum can only increase a^d+b^d; its maximum on
[k,2c-k] occurs at an endpoint by convexity. Thus the displayed mass
upper bound is correct. In particular r=k/c lies in [d/(d+1),1).

Direct differentiation gives exactly

    d/dr [3r^d/(1+r^d+(2-r)^d)]
      =3d r^(d-1)[1+2(2-r)^(d-1)]
                     /(1+r^d+(2-r)^d)^2>0.

Substituting r=d/(d+1) yields the claimed constant. The denominator is
strictly below 5 because Gamma_d<1 and (1+1/(d+1))^d<e<3. The factorial
geometric-series estimate of e<3 is valid, with strictness from j>=3.
Thus the stated >3Gamma_d/5>Gamma_d/2 margin is correct. At d=2 the
exact expression is 12/29.

## 5. Boundary and dependency findings

There is no untracked affine or lattice transformation, approximation,
measure limit, variational minimizer, or numerical inference. The only
external ordinary results used are section BM, full-body BM with its
positive-volume equality characterization, Fubini, and ordinary Grünbaum.
The theorem does not invoke a mixed-integer Grünbaum theorem.

No mathematical correction is required. A stronger separate finite-tilt
argument removes the need for endpoint properness and yields an explicit
quantitative result; it is documented separately in
`candidate fee4b98d94ecbcf2`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
